question.problem:
If the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{k}\cdot {10}^{1+x/2}+1$ has an inverse function given by 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=2\operatorname{log}⁡(1-x)-2,
$$

 
what is the value of $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{k}\cdot {10}^{1+x/2}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{k}\cdot {10}^{1+y/2}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{k}\cdot {10}^{1+y/2}+1 \\ \frac{1}{k}\cdot {10}^{1+y/2} & =x-1 \\ {10}^{1+y/2} & =kx-k \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{1+y/2}) & =\operatorname{log}⁡(kx-k) \\ 1+\frac{y}{2} & =\operatorname{log}⁡(kx-k) \\ \frac{y}{2} & =\operatorname{log}⁡(kx-k)-1 \\ y & =2\operatorname{log}⁡(kx-k)-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=2\operatorname{log}⁡(kx-k)-2.$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-1.$
